import datetime
from typing import Optional

def next_billing_date(start: datetime.date, months_ahead: int) -> datetime.date:
    """
    Calculate the billing date `months_ahead` months after `start`, keeping the same day-of-month.
    
    Handles edge cases where the target month has fewer days than the start month
    by rolling to the last day of the target month.
    
    Args:
        start: The starting date
        months_ahead: Number of months to add (must be non-negative)
        
    Returns:
        The billing date `months_ahead` months after `start`
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If months_ahead is negative
    """
    if months_ahead < 0:
        raise ValueError("months_ahead must be non-negative")
    
    if months_ahead == 0:
        return start
    
    # Calculate the target year and month
    target_year = start.year + (start.month + months_ahead - 1) // 12
    target_month = (start.month + months_ahead - 1) % 12 + 1
    
    # Determine the last day of the target month
    if target_month == 12:
        next_month_first_day = datetime.date(target_year + 1, 1, 1)
    else:
        next_month_first_day = datetime.date(target_year, target_month + 1, 1)
    
    last_day_of_target_month = next_month_first_day - datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    
    # Use the same day-of-month, but cap at the last day of the target month
    target_day = min(start.day, last_day_of_target_month.day)
    
    return datetime.date(target_year, target_month, target_day)

# Test cases to verify edge cases
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test case 1: Normal case (same month length)
    d1 = datetime.date(2023, 1, 15)
    result1 = next_billing_date(d1, 1)
    assert result1 == datetime.date(2023, 2, 15)
    
    # Test case 2: January to February (shorter month)
    d2 = datetime.date(2023, 1, 31)
    result2 = next_billing_date(d2, 1)
    assert result2 == datetime.date(2023, 2, 28)
    
    # Test case 3: Leap year February to March
    d3 = datetime.date(2020, 2, 29)
    result3 = next_billing_date(d3, 1)
    assert result3 == datetime.date(2020, 3, 29)
    
    # Test case 4: Non-leap year February to March
    d4 = datetime.date(2023, 2, 28)
    result4 = next_billing_date(d4, 1)
    assert result4 == datetime.date(2023, 3, 28)
    
    # Test case 5: Multiple months with month boundary crossing
    d5 = datetime.date(2023, 11, 30)
    result5 = next_billing_date(d5, 3)
    assert result5 == datetime.date(2024, 2, 29)  # 2024 is leap year
    
    # Test case 6: Year rollover
    d6 = datetime.date(2023, 12, 15)
    result6 = next_billing_date(d6, 2)
    assert result6 == datetime.date(2024, 2, 15)
    
    # Test case 7: Zero months ahead
    d7 = datetime.date(2023, 6, 15)
    result7 = next_billing_date(d7, 0)
    assert result7 == datetime.date(2023, 6, 15)
    
    # Test case 8: Large number of months
    d8 = datetime.date(2023, 1, 31)
    result8 = next_billing_date(d8, 24)
    assert result8 == datetime.date(2025, 1, 31)
    
    print("All test cases passed!")
